thread:
elena: quick sync — we need a pragmatic protection layer for routes hitting p99 blowups during bursts. saw multiple regressions where long-context + big microbatches pushed GPUs into slow kernel paths and KV cache churned the tail. proposing server-side per-route max_tokens and a soft-truncate policy that favors finishing earlier generations when p95 > SLO. thoughts?

sam: +1 on route caps. can we make it dynamic so we don't throttle steady-state high-throughput customers?

elena: yes, dynamic. idea: continuous profiler reports p95/p99 per model+route; an autoscaler agent adjusts max_tokens_target and microbatch_size ceilings. not a hard kill at first — start with soft truncation and token-shedding heuristics.

jia: FYI KV cache is the biggest tail culprit for >8k contexts. when we evict and reload kv pages during a microbatch, one request can block kernels and blow up others in the same batch. we should bias batching to keep long-context requests in isolated microbatches.

perf-bot: profile-summary: route=/chat/long-context model=gptx-6b p95=420ms p99=1.9s mean=210ms microbatch=16 kv-miss-rate=0.18 kernel-path=slow-attn

maria: what about admitting a smaller token budget up-front? e.g. client sees a 2048 -> 1024 cap notice and can request longer via streaming continuation. that keeps latency and still allows completeness for clients that accept follow-ups. :thinking_face: 

sam: kernel fallback: for certain sequence-lengths we should prefer a fast approximate kernel (quantized) at the tail instead of waiting for the exact high-precision path. customers who care about fidelity can pin route to exact kernel. default favors latency.

tim: UX question — how will this surface to devs? want minimal breaking changes. can we expose headers like `x-redwood-max-tokens` and `x-redwood-truncation-reason` so SDKs can auto-retry with streaming?

elena: plan: server enforces `max_tokens_effective` per request. if request.max_tokens > effective -> server responds with `200` + truncated content and header `x-redwood-truncated: true` and body includes "truncation_hint": "server_cap". SDKs should auto-continue with `continuation=true`. no client change required for most users but provide opt-out. example route config: 
```
route_config:
  name: chat-long-context
  slo_p95_ms: 300
  max_tokens_base: 2048
  max_tokens_dynamic: {
    scale_down_p95_ms: 450
    min_tokens: 512
  }
  isolate_long_context_requests: true
  prefer_latency_kernel: true
```

jia: that config looks good. need to add a KV isolation flag in the router so we don't pack >1 long-context into same microbatch. can we label requests with `context_bucket=long|short` at ingress?

elena: yes, ingress will tag. router heuristics: pack short+short up to microbatch cap, isolate long into single-request microbatches when p95 deviation > threshold.

maria: mitigation idea: token-shedding policy that truncates earliest non-essential tokens (system/meta) rather than user text. keep last N tokens of user history for coherence. this reduces KL surprises vs chopping from the front.

sam: NB: quantized fast-kernel causes subtle output drift on some evaluation prompts. we should gate automatic kernel fallback behind per-route eval pass (small eval set) and a rollback on quality alerts.

perf-bot: rollout metrics to watch: route.p95_ms, route.p99_ms, drop_rate_truncated, completion_rate_streaming_continuations, kv_miss_rate. deploy test will collect per-token cost delta too.

ops-bot: canary window scheduled: canary=10% traffic -> 1hr -> monitor p95/p99 & errors -> roll to 50% if stable. will create the canary job after we land config flags.

tim: also add telemetry for `truncation_hint` distribution and which tokens were removed (category tags only, no user data). important for product to avoid regressions.

devx: docs note: need to document server-enforced caps, headers, SDK behavior for auto-continuations and examples for best-effort streaming. I'll draft SDK changes once API headers finalized.

elena: action items: 1) eng-runtime: implement `max_tokens_dynamic` scaler + router isolation label (sam, jia) 2) perf: add canary profiler and gating eval (perf-bot -> sam) 3) ops: canary job and alert thresholds (ops-bot) 4) devx/docs: header + SDK patterns (devx). I'll open a PR with the config proto and a simulation script. anyone want to run quick sim with real traces?

jia: I can run 6h sim against last week's p99 spike trace and test isolation heuristics.

sam: I'll prototype the fast-kernel fallback with per-route eval harness. want to measure correctness deltas.

elena: great. ping me on PR. thanks all :thumbsup:
